subject: Urology
title: Scrotal Swelling
subtitle: Epididymo-orchitis, varicocele, hydrocele, spermatocele, testicular tumors, torsion and cryptorchidism
sourceNote: Built only from the uploaded SCROTAL SWELLING 3 lecture. The bank preserves the lecture definitions, figures, percentages, classifications, timings and treatment statements without adding external guideline details.

cases.title: Painful Febrile Scrotal Swelling
cases.scenario: A patient presents with scrotal pain and swelling associated with fever and malaise. The clinician is considering an inflammatory condition involving both the epididymis and testis.
cases.ar: مريض عنده scrotal pain وswelling مع fever وmalaise، والطبيب شاكك في التهاب الـepididymis والtestis.
questions: What is the most likely diagnosis?
State the bacterial and viral causes listed in the lecture.
Outline treatment.
How long should antibiotics continue in bacterial disease?
answer: Epididymo-orchitis.
Bacterial causes include E. coli, Neisseria gonorrhea and Chlamydia trachomatis; the listed viral cause is mumps.
Rest and scrotal support, anti-inflammatory drugs, analgesics, antipyretics, and antibiotics for bacterial epididymo-orchitis.
The antibiotic course should continue for two weeks.
cases.trap: The lecture emphasizes that epididymo-orchitis must be differentiated from testicular torsion, a true urologic emergency.
cases.memory: Pain + swelling + fever = think epididymo-orchitis, but exclude torsion.

cases.title: Parotiditis Followed by Orchitis
cases.scenario: A young patient develops scrotal pain and swelling about one week after parotid swelling.
cases.ar: مريض ظهر عنده scrotal pain وswelling بعد parotiditis بحوالي أسبوع.
questions: What is the likely cause?
What temporal relationship is stated in the lecture?
State the supportive treatment.
answer: Mumps orchitis.
Parotiditis may precede the onset of mumps orchitis by about one week.
Rest, scrotal support, anti-inflammatory drugs, analgesics and antipyretics.
cases.trap: Do not add antibiotics automatically to a viral cause unless bacterial epididymo-orchitis is present.
cases.memory: Mumps: parotiditis first, orchitis about one week later.

cases.title: Infertile Man with Dilated Scrotal Veins
cases.scenario: An infertile man has dilated tortuous scrotal veins that become more prominent with straining. Doppler shows venous diameters above 2-3 mm and reversed flow during Valsalva.
cases.ar: رجل بيعاني من infertility وعنده dilated tortuous scrotal veins بتزيد مع straining، والDoppler فيه veins أكبر من 2-3 mm وreversed flow مع Valsalva.
questions: What is the diagnosis?
Define the condition.
State the Doppler findings.
List the indications for varicocelectomy in the lecture.
answer: Varicocele.
Dilatation, elongation and tortuosity of the pampiniform plexus.
Dilated veins greater than 2-3 mm in diameter with reversed flow during Valsalva.
Infertility, testicular pain and testicular atrophy.
cases.trap: The lecture uses both clinical examination and Doppler; do not base grading on Doppler measurements.
cases.memory: Varicocele: tortuous pampiniform veins + Valsalva reflux.

cases.title: Visible Varicocele at Rest
cases.scenario: A patient has scrotal veins that are both visible and palpable while resting.
cases.ar: مريض عنده scrotal veins ظاهرة ومتحسسة وهو مرتاح.
questions: What clinical grade is this?
State all three clinical grades.
Why is varicocele more common on the left according to the lecture?
answer: Grade III varicocele.
Grade I: palpable only during straining. Grade II: not visible but palpable at rest. Grade III: visible and palpable at rest.
The left testicular vein joins the left renal vein at a right angle.
cases.trap: Grade II is palpable at rest but not visible; Grade III is both visible and palpable.
cases.memory: I strain, II feel at rest, III see and feel at rest.

cases.title: New Varicocele with Venous Obstruction
cases.scenario: A patient develops varicocele in association with obstruction of venous drainage from renal cell carcinoma with an IVC tumor thrombus.
cases.ar: مريض ظهر عنده varicocele بسبب obstruction للvenous drainage مع RCC وIVC tumor thrombus.
questions: What mechanism of varicocele is illustrated?
State the other etiological mechanism in the lecture.
What investigations are listed for varicocele assessment?
answer: Obstruction of venous drainage.
Retrograde reflux of venous blood into the pampiniform plexus due to incompetent valves.
Doppler ultrasound, semen analysis showing a stress pattern, and testosterone, LH, FSH and prolactin in severe oligospermia.
cases.trap: Do not assume every varicocele is due only to valve incompetence; the lecture includes venous obstruction.

cases.title: Infant with a Scrotal Fluid Swelling
cases.scenario: An infant has a painless scrotal fluid collection. Ultrasound shows a simple fluid-filled sac, and the swelling is considered infantile or congenital.
cases.ar: طفل عنده painless scrotal fluid swelling والUS موضح simple fluid collection sac، والاحتمال infantile أو congenital hydrocele.
questions: Define hydrocele using the processus vaginalis.
List the four clinical types.
How are infantile and congenital hydroceles treated during the first year?
What is done if the swelling persists?
answer: Hydrocele is accumulation of fluid in any part of the processus vaginalis.
Vaginal, infantile, congenital and hydrocele of the cord.
Observation, because many resolve during the first year.
Surgery is required if it persists.
cases.trap: The lecture separates childhood observation from adult vaginal hydrocele surgery.
cases.memory: Child hydrocele: observe in year one; persistent = surgery.

cases.title: Adult Vaginal Hydrocele
cases.scenario: An adult has a clinically diagnosed hydrocele, and ultrasound demonstrates a simple fluid collection sac around the testis.
cases.ar: شخص بالغ عنده hydrocele والUS موضح simple fluid collection حوالين الخصية.
questions: What type is most likely in this adult scenario?
What investigation finding supports the diagnosis?
State the treatment given in the lecture.
answer: Vaginal hydrocele.
Ultrasound shows a simple fluid collection sac.
Surgical eversion of the tunica vaginalis.
cases.trap: Do not apply the first-year observation rule to the lecture treatment of vaginal hydrocele.
cases.memory: Vaginal hydrocele = eversion of tunica vaginalis.

cases.title: Small Swelling Above the Testis
cases.scenario: A small painless swelling is discovered incidentally superior to the testicle. Ultrasound confirms a cystic lesion arising from the epididymal head.
cases.ar: في small painless swelling اتلاقت بالصدفة فوق الخصية، والUS أكد cystic lesion من head of epididymis.
questions: What is the diagnosis?
Define it and state its origin.
What is the role of ultrasound?
When is surgery indicated?
answer: Spermatocele.
A cystic accumulation of sperms arising from the head of the epididymis; it may be due to aneurysmal dilatation of an epididymal ductule.
Ultrasound confirms the diagnosis and rules out additional testicular pathology.
Spermatocelectomy is indicated for pain or progressive enlargement that bothers the patient.
cases.trap: A spermatocele is superior to the testicle and arises from the epididymal head.

cases.title: Painful Progressive Spermatocele
cases.scenario: A previously small spermatocele becomes painful and progressively enlarged, causing discomfort. The patient asks for needle aspiration.
cases.ar: مريض عنده spermatocele كبرت تدريجيًا وبقت مؤلمة، وبيسأل عن needle aspiration.
questions: What treatment is indicated?
Why should needle aspiration be avoided?
What two problems may follow aspiration according to the lecture?
answer: Spermatocelectomy.
Needle aspiration should be avoided.
It may cause infection or spillage of irritating sperms.
cases.trap: Needle aspiration is specifically discouraged in the lecture.

cases.title: Painless Firm Intratesticular Mass
cases.scenario: A 28-year-old man presents with painless scrotal swelling. Examination reveals a firm non-tender mass within the testis.
cases.ar: رجل 28 سنة عنده painless scrotal swelling وfirm non-tender mass جوه الخصية.
questions: What should this mass be considered until proven otherwise?
List the tumor markers.
State the ultrasound and CT investigations.
Outline treatment stated in the lecture.
answer: Testicular cancer.
AFP, beta-hCG and LDH.
Ultrasound: a homogeneous hypoechoic mass. CT scan of abdomen, pelvis and chest.
Radical orchiectomy; radiotherapy for radiosensitive seminoma; chemotherapy is recommended for non-seminoma tumors.
cases.trap: Any solid firm intratesticular mass should be treated as cancer until proven otherwise.
cases.memory: Firm painless intratesticular mass = cancer until proved otherwise.

cases.title: Small Tumor with Early Blood Spread
cases.scenario: A patient has a small testicular tumor but already has hematogenous metastases to distant organs.
cases.ar: مريض عنده small testicular tumor لكن حصل early hematogenous metastasis.
questions: Which pathological type is described?
List the blood-spread sites stated in the lecture.
State the usual lymphatic drainage pathway of the testis.
answer: Choriocarcinoma.
Lung, liver, brain, bone, kidney and adrenal.
Para-aortic lymph nodes, then cisterna chyli, thoracic duct and left supraclavicular lymph node (Virchow gland).
cases.trap: The lecture says blood spread is rare except in choriocarcinoma.
cases.memory: Choriocarcinoma = small tumor, early hematogenous spread.

cases.title: Sudden Severe Scrotal Pain with High Testis
cases.scenario: An adolescent presents with sudden severe scrotal pain, swelling, nausea and vomiting. The affected testis is higher than usual.
cases.ar: مراهق عنده sudden severe scrotal pain وswelling مع nausea وvomiting، والخصية high-riding.
questions: What is the diagnosis and mechanism?
How is it diagnosed?
What is the urgent treatment?
State the 6-hour and 24-hour timing statements.
answer: Testicular torsion; twisting of the spermatic cord cuts off blood supply to the testis.
Primarily by physical examination; Doppler ultrasound may confirm reduced blood flow.
Urgent surgical detorsion and orchiopexy.
It should be performed within 6 hours to save the testis; after 24 hours the testis can rarely be saved.
cases.trap: Torsion is a surgical emergency; investigation must not replace urgent intervention.
cases.memory: Sudden pain + high testis = detorsion and orchiopexy within 6 h.

cases.title: Manual Detorsion Before Theatre
cases.scenario: A clinician considers manual detorsion while arranging surgery for confirmed testicular torsion.
cases.ar: الطبيب بيفكر يعمل manual detorsion أثناء تجهيز المريض للجراحة.
questions: What is the role of manual detorsion?
Can it replace surgery?
What definitive operation remains required?
answer: Manual detorsion may be attempted in some cases.
No; it should not delay or replace surgical intervention.
Surgical detorsion and orchiopexy.
cases.trap: A successful manual maneuver does not cancel definitive surgery in the lecture pathway.
cases.memory: Manual detorsion: attempt only, never delay surgery.

cases.title: Child with an Empty Hemiscrotum
cases.scenario: A child has an empty hemiscrotum. The testis is not palpable on initial examination. The clinician examines the scrotum and inguinal canal in different positions and considers laparoscopy.
cases.ar: طفل عنده empty hemiscrotum والخصية impalpable، والطبيب بيفحص scrotum وinguinal canal في أوضاع مختلفة وبيفكر في laparoscopy.
questions: Define cryptorchidism and state its incidence.
Classify the impalpable testis.
State the examination principles in the lecture.
List the complications.
Outline treatment for an impalpable testis.
answer: Cryptorchidism is failure of one or both testes to descend into the scrotum; incidence is 3%.
Intra-abdominal testis, inguinal but atrophic testis, or absent/vanishing testis.
Warm the hands; examine the scrotum and inguinal canal; examine in supine, frog-leg or squatting positions.
Infertility, trauma, tumor and torsion.
Early surgical treatment before one year; laparoscopy can diagnose and may allow treatment in the same session.
cases.trap: Impalpable does not mean absent; the lecture includes intra-abdominal and atrophic inguinal testes.
cases.memory: Impalpable testis = laparoscopy for diagnosis and possible treatment.

cases.title: Palpable Mal-Descended Testis
cases.scenario: A child has a palpable testis outside the normal scrotal position. It can be manipulated from the groin into the scrotum in one examination.
cases.ar: طفل عنده testis palpable خارج مكانها الطبيعي، وفي الفحص ممكن تتحرك باليد من groin للscrotum.
questions: What diagnosis is suggested by the ability to move it into the scrotum?
List the palpable categories.
List the ectopic sites in the lecture.
State the operative treatment for a true undescended testis.
answer: Retractile testis.
Retractile testis, undescended testis and ectopic testis.
Superficial inguinal pouch, base of penis, perineum and femoral canal.
Orchiopexy with fixation in a scrotal sub-dartos pouch and herniotomy for an associated hernia sac.
cases.trap: Retractile testis can be moved into the scrotum; ectopic testis lies outside the normal descent pathway.
cases.memory: Retractile moves down; ectopic sits off-route.

coreShorts.q: Define scrotal swelling and state the urgent warning given in the lecture.
a: Scrotal swelling is abnormal enlargement of the scrotum indicating an underlying condition.
Immediate medical attention is needed when swelling is accompanied by sudden severe pain.

coreShorts.q: Define epididymo-orchitis and name the emergency from which it must be differentiated.
a: Inflammation of the epididymis and testicle.
It must be differentiated from testicular torsion, a true urologic emergency.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the causes of epididymo-orchitis listed in the lecture.
a: Bacterial: E. coli, Neisseria gonorrhea and Chlamydia trachomatis.
Viral: mumps.

coreShorts.q: State the clinical picture of epididymo-orchitis.
a: Scrotal pain and swelling.
Fever and malaise.

coreShorts.q: What is the relation between parotiditis and mumps orchitis?
coreShorts.a: Parotiditis may precede the onset of mumps orchitis by about one week.

coreShorts.q: Outline treatment of epididymo-orchitis and state antibiotic duration.
a: Rest and scrotal support.
Anti-inflammatory drugs, analgesics and antipyretics.
Antibiotics for bacterial epididymo-orchitis for two weeks.

coreShorts.q: Define varicocele and give its lecture prevalence figures.
a: Dilatation, elongation and tortuosity of the pampiniform plexus.
20% of the general population and 40% of infertile men.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the etiological mechanisms of varicocele.
a: Retrograde venous reflux due to incompetent valves.
Obstruction of venous drainage, such as renal cell carcinoma with IVC tumor thrombus.

coreShorts.q: Why is varicocele more common on the left side?
coreShorts.a: The left testicular vein joins the left renal vein at a right angle.

coreShorts.q: Describe the clinical examination finding in varicocele.
coreShorts.a: Dilated tortuous veins may be visible or palpable and show an impulse on straining.

coreShorts.q: State the clinical grading of varicocele.
a: Grade I: palpable only during straining.
Grade II: not visible but palpable at rest.
Grade III: visible and palpable at rest.

coreShorts.q: List the investigations for varicocele and the key Doppler findings.
a: Doppler ultrasound: veins greater than 2-3 mm and reversed flow with Valsalva.
Semen analysis: stress pattern.
Testosterone, LH, FSH and prolactin in severe oligospermia.

coreShorts.q: What are the indications for varicocelectomy?
a: Infertility.
Testicular pain.
Testicular atrophy.

coreShorts.q: Explain the embryological basis and definition of hydrocele.
a: The peritoneal bulge into the inguinal canal is the processus vaginalis.
It normally obliterates, while the part adjacent to the testis becomes tunica vaginalis.
Hydrocele is fluid accumulation in any part of the processus vaginalis.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the clinical types of hydrocele.
a: Vaginal hydrocele.
Infantile hydrocele.
Congenital hydrocele.
Hydrocele of the cord.

coreShorts.q: How is hydrocele diagnosed?
a: Clinical examination.
Ultrasound shows a simple fluid collection sac.

coreShorts.q: State treatment of infantile and congenital hydrocele.
a: Observe during the first year because many resolve.
If it persists, surgery is required.

coreShorts.q: State treatment of vaginal hydrocele.
coreShorts.a: Surgical eversion of the tunica vaginalis.

coreShorts.q: Define spermatocele and state its origin.
a: Cystic accumulation of sperms.
It arises from the head of the epididymis and may result from aneurysmal dilatation of an epididymal ductule.

coreShorts.q: Describe the presentation and diagnosis of spermatocele.
a: Usually an incidentally discovered small swelling superior to the testicle.
Ultrasound confirms the diagnosis and rules out additional testicular pathology.

coreShorts.q: State the indication for spermatocelectomy and explain why aspiration is avoided.
a: Surgery is indicated for pain or progressive enlargement that bothers the patient.
Aspiration may cause infection or spillage of irritating sperms.

coreShorts.q: State the age association and cryptorchidism risk for primary testicular tumors.
a: They are the most common solid malignant tumor in men aged 20-35 years.
Undescended testis carries five times the risk stated in the lecture.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the pathological types and one key feature of each.
a: Seminoma: commonest testicular neoplasm.
Teratoma: arises from totipotent cells differentiating into ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.
Choriocarcinoma: small tumor with early hematogenous spread.
Leydig cell tumor: produces excess androgens.
Sertoli cell tumor: rare and occurs after puberty.

coreShorts.q: Describe the routes of spread of testicular tumors.
a: Lymphatic spread to para-aortic nodes, cisterna chyli, thoracic duct and left supraclavicular node.
Blood spread is rare except in choriocarcinoma, which spreads to lung, liver, brain, bone, kidney and adrenal.
Local spread occurs late.

coreShorts.q: What rule applies to a solid firm intratesticular mass?
coreShorts.a: It should be considered testicular cancer until proven otherwise.

coreShorts.q: State the clinical presentation and tumor markers of testicular cancer.
a: Painless scrotal swelling.
Firm non-tender testicular mass.
AFP, beta-hCG and LDH.

coreShorts.q: State the imaging studies for testicular cancer.
a: Ultrasound: homogeneous hypoechoic mass.
CT of the abdomen, pelvis and chest.

coreShorts.q: Outline treatment of testicular tumors in the lecture.
a: Radical orchiectomy.
Radiotherapy because seminoma is radiosensitive.
Chemotherapy for non-seminoma tumors.

coreShorts.q: Define testicular torsion and state its presentation.
a: Twisting of the spermatic cord cuts off blood supply.
Sudden severe scrotal pain and swelling, sometimes nausea and vomiting, with a high-riding testis.

coreShorts.q: How is testicular torsion diagnosed?
a: Primarily by physical examination.
Doppler ultrasound may confirm reduced testicular blood flow.

coreShorts.q: State urgent management and timing in testicular torsion.
a: Urgent surgical detorsion and orchiopexy within six hours.
After 24 hours, the testis can rarely be saved.
Manual detorsion may be attempted but must not delay surgery.

coreShorts.q: Define cryptorchidism and state its incidence and prematurity figures.
a: Failure of one or both testes to descend into the scrotum.
Incidence: 3%.
Premature infants: 30% versus 3% in full-term babies.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the risk factors for cryptorchidism listed in the lecture.
a: Premature birth.
Low birth weight.
Family history.
Developmental conditions such as Down syndrome or abdominal wall defects.

coreShorts.q: Classify palpable mal-descended testes and list ectopic sites.
a: Palpable testes represent 80% and include retractile, undescended and ectopic testes.
Ectopic sites: superficial inguinal pouch, base of penis, perineum and femoral canal.

coreShorts.q: Classify the impalpable testis and summarize examination, complications and treatment.
a: Impalpable testes represent 20%: intra-abdominal, inguinal but atrophic, or absent/vanishing.
Warm hands; examine scrotum and inguinal canal in supine, frog-leg or squatting positions.
Complications: infertility, trauma, tumor and torsion.
Early surgery before one year; orchiopexy in a sub-dartos pouch with herniotomy; laparoscopy for impalpable testis.
